reason: Conversation 1 firmly rejects the DIY regas kit and reaches the right diagnosis. It treats the oily mark on the pipe as evidence of a sealed-system leak, tells the customer to stop running the fridge and call a qualified technician, and raises replacement as an option. Conversation 2 states the flammable-gas danger more clearly, but it pushes an iced-evaporator and defrost theory and a 24-hour defrost, even though the customer had reported no frost. It never asks about oil marks or damage, ends abruptly with a vague 'compressor or leak' verdict, and says nothing about whether repair is worth the cost. Conversation 1 does not stress that R600a is flammable and makes some overstated claims, but its overall guidance served the homeowner better.
